Hi Caleb — thanks for the clear asks. Quick summary and an operational proposal so legal/procurement can slot this into the SOW/DPA amendment.

What we currently offer (baseline):
- Backups: automated daily snapshots, default snapshot retention 90 days for full backups; cold archive beyond 90 days is available as an add-on.
- Logs: request-level logs (request metadata + headers) are retained for 30 days by default; full payload retention is opt-in and scoped per-account.
- Subprocessors: we maintain a published subprocessor list, with >30 days notice for significant changes; routine infra provider rotations are documented in the change log.

Proposed temporary operational path (what we can commit to now):
1) Purge-freeze request: customer files a ticket to secure@redwood.ai and marks the case type "purge-freeze" + attaches legal hold paperwork.
2) Default freeze window: 14 days (automated), with documented extensions granted in 30-day increments up to 180 days with legal justification and executive approval.
3) Forensic snapshot: we can produce a read-only forensic snapshot within 48 hours of approval; snapshot access is audited and limited to named accounts.
4) Log retention exception: we can enable a 90-day payload retention for audit purposes as an add-on; we strongly prefer field-level redaction or tokenization for PII-sensitive fields.

Next steps I recommend:
- Kimberly to review and provide required DPA redlines and any additional contract language for the purge-freeze flow.
- Rishi to coordinate procurement (SOW amendment + billing for extended retention).

I've attached a draft schedule showing how the freeze interacts with our purge cadence and the export we can provide for subprocessor disclosure.

Attachments: backup_purge_schedule_v1.xlsx, subprocessor_export_20260512.csv

If that mapping looks OK, we can schedule a short call with MedCura legal tomorrow to walk through justification and signature process.

—Olga

Caleb, Olga,

Thanks for the draft operational path — helpful. A few legal points and a small redline set attached. Key items from legal review:

- Purge-freeze authorization: legal needs a clause that defines acceptable triggers (regulatory subpoena, litigation hold, incident response) and requires an authorized MedCura signer for extensions beyond 30 days.
- Data minimization: we will not accept unredacted full payload retention by default. Please provide technical options for pseudonymization or field-level redaction and confirm whether the retained artifacts will be accessible to Redwood support staff.
- Subprocessor notice: we need explicit language that any onboarding of subprocessors who have access to production backups requires a 30-day notice plus an objection process; if Redwood cannot provide 30 days' notice, MedCura reserves the right to terminate that subprocessor's access or require on-premise-only handling.

I've attached our redlines (dpa_redlines_medcura.pdf) and included inline comments on the proposed freeze durations. For SOC2 artifacts: Olga, please attach your most recent SOC2 Type II report or provide a link to the read-only evidence bundle. We will need that to close the procurement security review.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
